This filing records allotment/share changes and is separate from an application to increase issued share capital.

title: How to register a company charge or mortgage with CAC
summary: The CAC post-incorporation filing for registering a mortgage, debenture or other registrable company charge, using the instrument that creates the charge and any court extension order or existing-charge certificate that applies.
feeNote: The charge depends on the transaction and applicable CAC filing rules. Confirm the official amount in the filing workflow before payment.
timeline: CAC publishes a 12-working-hour timeline for mortgages, debentures and charges after receipt of a complete submission or compliance with any issued query.
requirements: A copy of the executed instrument that creates the mortgage, debenture or other registrable charge
A copy of the certificate for the existing charge when the filing is an upstamping and that certificate is available
A copy of the court order extending the time to register the charge when the filing is outside the ordinary statutory period
The registered company's CAC record and transaction information needed to identify the secured obligation and charge
steps: Prepare the executed instrument creating the charge and determine whether the filing is a new charge, an upstamping or a late registration backed by a court extension.
Sign in to CAC's official portal and open the post-incorporation filing for mortgages, debentures or company charges.
Enter the charge particulars and upload the creating instrument plus the existing-charge certificate or court extension order when either applies.
Review the filing, pay the official CAC charge generated for the transaction and submit the completed application.
Monitor the filing for approval or a CAC query and retain the registered charge evidence with the underlying finance and security documents.
notes: CAC's checklist treats mortgages, debentures, bills of sale and other loan-security charges within the charge-registration family.
A court order is specifically relevant when extra time to register the charge has been obtained.
Use the Deed of Release or Satisfaction guide after a registered charge has been discharged.

title: How to register satisfaction or release of a company charge with CAC
summary: The CAC filing for recording that a registered company charge has been released or satisfied, using the duly executed stamped Deed of Release and the existing charge record.
feeLabel: Deed of Release filing fee applies
feeNote: Confirm the current CAC charge generated for the Deed of Release or satisfaction filing before payment.
timeline: CAC publishes a 12-working-hour timeline for a Deed of Release after receipt of a complete submission or compliance with any issued query.
requirements: A stamped Deed of Release that has been duly executed by the relevant parties
Evidence of registration of the principal deed or charge when that evidence is available
The registered company's CAC record and the particulars needed to identify the charge being released
steps: Confirm the exact registered charge being discharged and obtain the stamped, duly executed Deed of Release from the relevant parties.
Sign in to CAC's official portal and start the post-incorporation filing for satisfaction of charge or Deed of Release.
Enter the charge details and upload the executed Deed of Release together with evidence of the principal charge registration when available.
Review the filing, pay the official CAC amount generated for the transaction and submit the application.
Monitor the filing for approval or a query and retain the updated CAC charge record as evidence that the release or satisfaction was registered.
notes: The Deed of Release must relate to the correct registered charge; verify the charge details before filing.
CAC's checklist lists evidence of registration of the principal deed as optional for this filing.
Registering the original charge and registering its later satisfaction are separate CAC transactions.

title: How voluntary striking-off of a company works with CAC
summary: The CAC process for a company seeking removal from the register when it has not commenced business and has no undischarged obligations, including the special resolution and public notice inviting objections.
feeNote: Confirm the current CAC filing amount in the official route before making payment; this guide does not treat voluntary striking-off as a substitute for formal winding-up.
requirements: A special resolution approving the application for the company to be struck off the register
Newspaper cuttings showing publication of the striking-off resolution in three national daily newspapers and inviting objections
A company that has not commenced business and has no undischarged obligations
Sufficient reasons for the striking-off request and no reasonable objection received within 28 days after the last publication
steps: Confirm that the company meets CAC's striking-off conditions, particularly that it has not commenced business and has no undischarged obligations.
Pass the special resolution for striking-off and publish the resolution in three national daily newspapers with an invitation for objections.
Allow the objection period to run and keep the newspaper cuttings that prove the required publications.
Sign in to CAC's official portal and submit the striking-off application with the resolution, publication evidence and reasons for the request, then pay the official filing charge.
Track the application and any objection or CAC query, and do not represent the company as dissolved until the Commission completes the striking-off process.
notes: CAC's checklist says no reasonable objection must have been received within 28 days of the last newspaper publication.
Voluntary striking-off is not a notice of winding-up and should not be used to bypass outstanding company obligations.
Property and legal consequences can follow dissolution, so the company should preserve the final CAC record and professional advice used for the closure.

title: How to register herbal medicines and dietary supplements with NAFDAC
summary: The NAFDAC registration route for herbal medicines and dietary supplements made in Nigeria, using NAPAMS with company, brand, technical, label and laboratory evidence for each product.
feeNote: Use NAFDAC's current tariff or the amount generated through its official regulatory workflow for the exact herbal medicine or dietary-supplement application.
timeline: Depends on dossier completeness, product assessment, facility or GMP status, laboratory review and NAFDAC regulatory processing.
requirements: Evidence of business incorporation with the Corporate Affairs Commission for the applicant
A contract-manufacturing agreement when the applicant owns the brand but uses another manufacturer
Evidence that the brand name is registered with Nigeria's Trademark Registry in the brand owner's name
A completed Herbal Medicine Technical Information Submission Template for the product
Product labels or artwork prepared to NAFDAC's herbal and dietary-supplement labelling guidance
A comprehensive Certificate of Analysis from the quality-control laboratory that tested or evaluated the product
steps: Open NAFDAC's current herbal-medicine and dietary-supplement registration guideline and prepare the listed company, brand, technical, label and laboratory documents.
Create or sign in to the official NAPAMS account and start a separate product-registration application for the herbal medicine or dietary supplement.
Complete the online product information and upload the application letter, incorporation evidence, brand documents, technical template, artwork and Certificate of Analysis.
Pay the official NAFDAC charge generated for the application and present original documents if NAFDAC requests them during review.
Track the application in NAPAMS, answer any regulatory or laboratory query and wait for approval before marketing the product as NAFDAC-registered.
notes: NAFDAC requires a separate registration application for each herbal medicine or dietary-supplement product.
The applicant should not treat a submitted NAPAMS application as approval to manufacture, advertise or sell an unregistered product.
Imported herbal remedies and supplements use a separate NAFDAC guideline and may have different evidence requirements.

A separate application for each pesticide product being registered
The product identity, manufacturer information and regulatory documents specified in NAFDAC's locally made pesticide guideline
Product labelling and technical or safety evidence needed for NAFDAC to evaluate the pesticide category
Official payment evidence generated through the NAFDAC application route

title: How to register animal feed with NAFDAC

A contract-manufacturing agreement when another facility manufactures the product for the brand owner
Evidence that the brand name is registered with the Trademark Registry
Evidence of satisfactory facility inspection or the applicable GMP certificate for the product line
Product labels or artwork for the animal-feed product
A comprehensive Certificate of Analysis for the product

Track the application, answer any NAFDAC query and wait for the final registration decision before selling the feed as a registered product.
notes: NAFDAC requires a separate application for each animal-feed product.
The local-manufacturing route is different from the published route for imported animal feed.
A registration application does not replace the facility-inspection or product-quality evidence required by the guideline.
